Consider the following "normal" situation:

1) Card is destroyed.

First off, I think we can agree that in a normal situation the triggers won't happen between steps #2 and #3. If they do, I want a ruling saying this.

posts.name: dypaca
posts.cooked:
The trouble with changing it to "when this card would be destroyed" is that then the bounty 'No Executions' can't stop Sonic Mine or Explosive Wagon (they always have to be in play before 'No Executions').  Perhaps not a huge issue, but I'd always assumed that was half the point of that bounty.  If the goal is to resolve Explosive Wagon as the first reaction to its destruction, we almost need some new timing term like 'As this card is destroyed'.

Arenson, I think that summarizes the questions well.  Although I think I may have been the only one arguing the answer to I) could be 'yes', and upon further thought it seems like the answer really should be 'no'.  It occured to me that I'm quite certain cards like Cryo Bot or more importantly Isothermic Transducer can't react to the damage which kills them, so it would be really weird if cards can naturally stick around for reactions to their destruction but not reactions to the damage which caused that destruction.

Given that, I think I really prefer the old assumption that 'When this card is destroyed' always resolves from out of play, but if we are set on the card being in play when it resolves, then I guess the best option is that cards leave play differently if they say "When this card is destroyed".
